findings.title: Stock reservation atomicity broken - partial deductions on failure
findings.explanation: The original code validated all items had sufficient stock BEFORE modifying any inventory. The new code validates and deducts in the same loop, causing partial stock deductions when validation fails mid-loop. This leaves inventory in an inconsistent state.
findings.suggestion: Restore the pre-validation pattern: check all items have sufficient stock first, then deduct in a separate loop. Or use transactional semantics with rollback capability.
findings.trigger_condition: When reserve_many() is called with multiple SKUs where at least one SKU has insufficient stock after earlier SKUs in the iteration order

findings.title: Coupon minimum threshold logic inverted - exact match now rejected
findings.explanation: Changed from '<' to '<=' which incorrectly rejects coupons when subtotal exactly equals the minimum requirement. Original behavior allowed exact matches; new behavior rejects them.
findings.suggestion: Revert to '<' operator to maintain correct business logic where subtotal >= minimum_cents should satisfy the coupon requirement.
findings.trigger_condition: When applying a coupon where subtotal equals coupon.minimum_cents exactly
findings.evidence_snippet:
if subtotal <= coupon.minimum_cents:
            raise ValueError("coupon minimum not met")

findings.title: State mutation before full validation causes inconsistent inventory
findings.explanation: The original code validated ALL stock availability before any mutation (atomic validation). The new code validates and mutates incrementally within the loop. If reserving multiple SKUs where SKU A passes but SKU B fails, SKU A's stock is already deducted while SKU B raises an exception, leaving inventory in an inconsistent partially-committed state.
findings.suggestion: Restore the two-phase approach: validate all items first, then mutate all items. Or use a transaction pattern with rollback capability.
findings.trigger_condition: When reserve_many is called with multiple SKUs where an earlier SKU passes the stock check but a later SKU fails

findings.title: Partial state mutation in reserve_many causes data inconsistency
findings.explanation: The refactored reserve_many method now deducts stock inside the loop before validating all items. If validation fails partway through, earlier items have already had their stock reduced while the operation ultimately fails. This creates inconsistent inventory state.
findings.suggestion: Restore the two-phase approach: validate all quantities first, then modify stock. Keep the upfront validation check before the loop.
findings.trigger_condition: Stock modification occurs inside iteration loop without prior full validation

findings.title: Coupon minimum boundary condition incorrectly rejects valid orders
findings.explanation: Changed from '<' to '<=' means when subtotal equals exactly coupon.minimum_cents, the coupon is now rejected. Typically 'minimum not met' implies the order must be AT LEAST the minimum amount, so equality should satisfy the requirement. This breaks valid coupon usage at the exact boundary.
findings.suggestion: Revert to '<' operator so that subtotal >= minimum_cents allows the coupon, which matches typical business logic for minimum thresholds.
findings.trigger_condition: When order subtotal equals exactly coupon.minimum_cents
